Stories

The thing that got most of us through the door was hearing our own story come out of a stranger's mouth. This is a place for those.

Mine, in short

At 22 I couldn't do anything without a drink in my hand. I thought that was just what being young looked like, because everyone around me looked the same.

I got sober on November 12, 2014, at 29. The decade between 19 and 29 is the most expensive thing I own. I say that without self-pity. It's just the price, and I'd like you to have at 18 the information I had at 30.

What I didn't expect was what came next. Ski seasons. Skydiving. Hunting, travel, starting over more than once. Camping on a beach with the love of my life. The life I thought I was giving up turned out to be one I'd never had access to.

The Crossroads is the longer version of where it went wrong. A Life Worth Showing Up For is the longer version of where it went right.

Add yours

Somebody is sitting where you sat, looking for proof that a person like them gets out. A few honest paragraphs from you could be that proof.

First name, initials or a made-up one. Your choice.
What it was like, what changed, what it's like now. Please leave out other people's names.

Opening soon

Story submissions aren't open yet. In the meantime, the best place to tell it is out loud: at a meeting, to a mate, or to someone newer than you who needs to hear it.

If you write one, three prompts

  • What did a normal week look like before?
  • What was the moment, or the slow pile of moments, that changed it?
  • What can you do now that you couldn't then?
